title: Technical Art course wiki
summary: Follow the course by week, revisit a mechanism, or find a practical check for an asset you are investigating.

title: Maintaining the course wiki
summary: Add a week without duplicating explanations, losing evidence, or mixing a proposal with a confirmed course requirement.

title: Week 1 · Technical Art foundations
summary: Turn a production problem into an investigation that another person can understand and continue.

title: Week 2 · Assets, pipelines, and validation
summary: Follow a surface from Maya to Unreal, identify the data behind its appearance, and investigate a museum example with evidence.

title: Week 3 · Python, Maya automation, and artist-facing UI
summary: Read a small Python operation, automate a scoped texel-density repair in Maya, and make its state, scope, and evidence understandable to an artist.

title: Week 4 · Editor tool development
summary: Turn a useful check into an interface that an artist can operate and understand.

title: Week 5 · Applied math for Technical Artists
summary: Use mathematical relationships to explain concrete changes in position, orientation, and surface behavior.

title: Week 6 · Introduction to Technical Animation
summary: Connect motion and deformation to the asset relationships that make them work.

title: Week 7 · Midterm feedback and reflection
summary: Use evidence from the current work to choose the next improvement and explain what you learned.

title: Week 8 · Real-time rendering pipeline
summary: Open the rendering box that Week 2 deliberately kept simple.

title: Week 9 · Shaders and material systems
summary: Develop surface behavior and useful artist controls with an understanding of the rendering work involved.

title: Week 10 · Profiling and optimization
summary: Use measurements and controlled comparisons to evaluate quality and cost.

title: Week 11 · Procedural content and scalability
summary: Evaluate repeatable generation as a system with inputs, constraints, and artistic control.

title: Week 12 · Production systems and maintainability
summary: Prepare a tool or asset system for other people to use, revise, and continue.

title: Mesh anatomy
summary: Geometry, topology, normals, UVs, and assignments describe different parts of the same asset.

title: Normals and normal maps
summary: Distinguish face orientation, mesh shading directions, and sampled normal-map information before choosing a repair.

title: UVs and texture lookup
summary: The image stores values; coordinates determine where the surface reads them.

title: Texture data and interpretation
summary: A texture stores channel values. Its intended role determines how those values should be interpreted and used.

title: Materials and shaders
summary: A shader performs rendering calculations; a material defines surface logic and settings; textures can supply some of its inputs.

title: Maya-to-Unreal handoffs
summary: Follow identity, data, and dependencies through export, import, assignment, revision, and reimport.

title: Skeletal assets
summary: Separate the joint pose, the surface following that pose, and the animation being played.

title: Mips, mesh LOD, and streaming
summary: Several systems change what data is used at a distance. Identify which representation changed before explaining the result.

title: Validation and evidence
summary: A useful check compares observed data with an explicit requirement and explains the scope of its result.

title: Technical documentation
summary: Help another person understand the intended result, reproduce the test, verify the outcome, and maintain the example.

title: Museum investigation lab
summary: Observe first, choose a test with a reason, and leave evidence that another person can understand.

title: Create your own museum exhibit
summary: Make one technical idea observable through a clear comparison, a visitor question, and reproducible evidence.

title: Exhibit record template
summary: A compact starting point for a visitor explanation and a reproducible technical record.

title: Reading and visual library
summary: Choose a source by the question it answers, with practical references first and deeper theory available when it becomes useful.

title: Working glossary
summary: Short definitions tied to the inspection questions used in the course.
